title: Booking-time prediction of failed same-day discharge after elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy: development and temporal validation
abstract: Objective: to develop and temporally validate a booking-time model predicting failed same-day discharge after elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Design: retrospective development on 2019 to 2023 records and validation on 2024 to 2025 records at one hospital. Predictors: eight pre-specified booking-time variables including planned list position. Results and conclusions will be written after the analysis.
introduction: Many patients booked as day cases stay overnight after late conversion. Published models are mostly at high risk of bias and rarely validated, and charts record nausea poorly, although medication records offer a validated proxy.
methods: Penalised logistic regression with pre-specified predictors, bootstrap optimism correction, surgeon clustering in a sensitivity model, and temporal validation with calibration and decision curves. Nausea needing treatment is measured from rescue antiemetic doses, checked against sampled charts. TRIPOD reporting.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present the cohort flow, model coefficients, apparent and optimism-corrected performance, validation discrimination and calibration, and decision curves.
discussion: The discussion will consider how the unit could use the model at booking, the limits of the nausea proxy, practice drift and the non-causal meaning of list position.
limitations: One hospital; proxy measurement of nausea; list position partly chosen by risk.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim that moving patients on the list reduces overnight stays.
summary: TRIPOD-structured draft with results left empty.
